text:
alex: heads up — after rolling routing-policy-v2 to prod, console shows ~10% of quota as "unattributed" for a few tenants. looks like SDKs are still sending the legacy policy tag (x-rd-policy) in some paths :grimacing:

marie: ugh. which SDKs? any pattern in languages / client versions?

alex: initial scan -> mostly python 1.4.x and go 0.9.x clients used by internal platform services. ts clients on 2.0+ look fine. not all traffic, seems tied to streaming/stream-chunk paths.

sam: can we make console fallback to read both header names? quick fix for dashboards while we patch SDKs.

brian: we already tried a fallback but telemetry pipeline deduped by header name earlier in ingestion. changing that will affect sampling math. need to be careful.

marie: action plan proposal: 1) console/ingest add tolerant mapping that merges legacy->new for attribution only (no sampling changes), 2) patch python/go SDKs to emit new header name (x-rd-route-policy) in next patch release and include runtime guard for older server handshake, 3) add canary with 2% of traffic and watch quota attribution & cost.

alex: +1. timeline?

sam: I can land ingest mapping as a hotfix today if we accept slight additional CPU cost for the merge step. won't change sampling IDs, just mapping attribute key -> canonical key.

marie: please include a toggle flagged in console so we can flip back quickly. we should also add a metric: ingestion.mapped_legacy_policy_count.

brian: agree on telemetry metric. i'll add a short-lived counter and alert if mapped count spikes > 5% of total requests for > 10m.

alex: SDK patches: python needs minimal change. sample PR snippet: ```python
# old: headers['x-rd-policy'] = policy_id
# new: headers['x-rd-route-policy'] = policy_id
# fallback to legacy if server handshake indicates v1
headers['x-rd-route-policy'] = policy_id
if not server_supports_route_v2:
    headers['x-rd-policy'] = policy_id
```

marie: for TS we recommend only new header (we're seeing >=2.0 already), but include a compatibility test harness for local proxy testing.

sam: go patch is slightly uglier because internal http client reuses header map; i'll do a PR with atomic swap and add unit tests. plan to release python 1.4.1, go 0.9.3 and note minor non-breaking change.

tanya: what about client-side telemetry events? some customers rely on client-sent policy id for cost dashboards. we should update SDK changelogs to call it out and provide migration snippet.

marie: yes — add migration notes in dev portal and a console banner for affected tenants. set deprecation window 60 days.

alex: can we also add a quick QA checklist for the canary? key things: quota attribution parity, no regression in latency, no duplicate attributions, ingest mapped metric within expected bounds.

brian: + checklist. i'll wire up dashboards and a grafana panel for mapped_legacy_policy_count / total.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: ingest-hotfix-map-legacy -> prod-canary (2%). started rollout. :rocket:

marie: nice. once ingest hotfix is live we should run a smoke query for the affected tenants and confirm unattributed drops. alex can you run?

alex: on it. running ad-hoc: `SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE tenant = 'acme' AND policy_attribution = 'unattributed' AND ts > now() - interval '1 hour'`

alex: after 15m of canary: unattributed for acme down from 12% -> 1.4%. mapped_legacy_policy_count ~9.2% of total which aligns with the old gap. looks good so far.

tanya: ok to ship SDK patches after ingest fix fully rolled? we should make sure changelogs explicitly say: "set x-rd-route-policy header; old header retained as fallback for servers w/handshake v1; update by DATE"

sam: yes. i'll schedule SDK releases tomorrow morning. post-release we should monitor if any tenants still show >1% unattributed after 72h, then do outreach.

marie: excellent. please add short note to release PRs about required minute-level canary checks and the dashboards to look at. :memo:

alex: will follow up with final postmortem-like thread after full rollout. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
